{{Quote|The Shrine of Kooroo is certainly a mystery on Gelgelar.|Personal addendum by Platt Okeefe|<ref name="Platt" />}}
The '''Shrine of Kooroo''' located on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Gelgelar/Legends|Gelgelar]] was one of a series of [[Shrine of Kooroo|similar structures]] found on several worlds throughout known [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. An ancient building made out of the same type of stone as the other Shrines of Kooroo, the shrine on Gelgelar was considered especially unusual due to the extreme scarcity of naturally available stone on that world. The Shrine of Kooroo was a three-level structure overgrown by [[Plant/Legends|plants]] and [[Fungus/Legends|fungi]], and was flanked by at least two stone obelisks.

When a group of [[Colonist/Legends|settlers]] arrived on Gelgelar 250 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the arrivals camped near the Shrine of Kooroo, which was the only existing structure on the planet at the [[Time/Legends|time]] and was located on the only hill for [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] around. Eventually, the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[City/Legends|settlement]] known as the [[Gelgelar Free Port/Legends|Gelgelar Free Port]] formed around the shrine, and at some point the [[Force-sensitive]] [[Hermit/Legends|hermit]] known as the [[Wise Man of Kooroo]] came to reside inside the structure.

By the time of the Galactic Civil War, the Wise Man of Kooroo was occasionally visited at the shrine by [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] as well as members of the cult known as the [[Fellowship of Kooroo]]. The latter engaged on a [[Pilgrimage of Kooroo|pilgrimage]] to the various Shrines of Kooroo, which they believed were connected to the Fellowship's spiritual leader, [[Kooroo (being)|Kooroo]]. Such visitors provided the Wise Man, who was never seen leaving the shrine, with offerings of [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]], and the pilgrims would [[Meditation/Legends|meditate]] and converse with the hermit during their visits to the sanctuary. On one occasion, [[Professor/Legends|Professor]] [[Reina Solov]] hired a group of individuals to visit the Wise Man of Kooroo at the shrine and determine facts about the structure's origin. By [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], it was believed by [[Scholar/Legends|scholars]] that the Shrines of Kooroo had been built by an advanced [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] known as the [[Kooroo (species)|Kooroo]], and it was thought the structures may have served to facilitate interstellar [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] communication or even teleportation.

==Description==
{{Quote|Shrines of Kooroo have been uncovered on several Outer Rim worlds, including Haffrin, Gelgelar, Branteez, Sufezz, and Boztrok.|TriNebulon News report by Andor Javin|<ref name="Journal13">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>}}
The Shrine of Kooroo on the<ref name="Platt" /> [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Gelgelar system/Legends|Gelgelar system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Gelgelar/Legends|Gelgelar]] was a<ref name="Platt" /> round<ref name="Journal13 Shrines">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}} &mdash; Based on physical and historical characteristics common to all [[Shrine of Kooroo|Shrines of Kooroo]]</ref> three-level building, with the two lower levels enclosed and the uppermost level consisting of a roof raised on four pillars over a<ref name="Platt" /> round<ref name="Journal14 Shrines" /> solid structure.<ref name="Platt" /> The form of the building was similar to that of other [[Shrine of Kooroo|Shrines of Kooroo]], located on several worlds<ref name="Journal14 Shrines" /> throughout known [[Realspace/Legends|space]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and it was entirely made out of brown stone<ref name="Platt" />&mdash;the same type of stone used in the construction of the other shrines. In addition, similarly to the other Shrines of Kooroo, which were usually surrounded by a series of stone obelisks,<ref name="Journal14 Shrines" /> the shrine on Gelgelar also had in its vicinity two such structures.<ref name="Platt" />

[[File:GelgelarFreePortMap-PlattStarport.png|thumb|right|200px|The Shrine of Kooroo lay at the highest point in the Gelgelar Free Port.]]
By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the exterior of the Shrine of Kooroo was covered in [[Moss/Legends|moss]], [[Fungus/Legends|fungi]], and molds, which all flourished in the [[Temperature/Legends|cool]], [[Water/Legends|damp]] climate of Gelgelar. The [[Plant/Legends|vegetation]] had reached the roof at the very top of the central shrine and had entirely blanketed one of its satellite obelisks. As a result, through the planet's fog, the structure frequently resembled a giant hill of fungus with an opening and a few right angles. Rainwater dripped between the stones of the shrine, reaching its interior.<ref name="Platt" />

The Shrine of Kooroo was situated at the top of the only hill for [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] around. When the [[City/Legends|settlement]] known as the [[Gelgelar Free Port/Legends|Gelgelar Free Port]] formed around the shrine, the shrine came to be located at the highest point in the town and was the only building in the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] made out of stone. The shrine was generally considered an oddity due to the material used in its construction, since stone was extremely rare on Gelgelar<ref name="Platt" /> and only occurred as part of the bedrock several [[Meter/Legends|meters]] or even tens of meters underground.<ref name="Journal14">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}}</ref>

==History==
===An ancient structure===
{{Quote|One theory is that the shrines served the Kooroo civilization as a kind of communication network, boosting their telepathic powers enough to overcome vast interstellar distances. This is an intriguing theory, but evidence is lacking.|Lecture by Dr. Corellia Antilles|<ref name="Journal14" />}}
Although the identity and fate of the builders of the Gelgelar Shrine of Kooroo were unknown,<ref name="Platt" /> general consensus among [[Scholar/Legends|scholars]]<ref name="Journal14" /> by [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]]<ref name="11 ABY">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}} is set "shortly after the re-establishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]" following the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final death]] of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]].</ref> was that the Shrines of Kooroo&mdash;many of whom were estimated to have been built more than twenty [[Millennium/Legends|thousand years]] prior&mdash;were constructed by an advanced [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] known as the [[Kooroo (species)|Kooroo]]. The purpose of the structures was still unclear by that time, however, with various theories claiming that the shrines were used by the aliens for interstellar [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] communication or even teleportation.<ref name="Journal14" />

A group of criminals, escaped [[Politics/Legends|political]] [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]], and vagabonds arrived on Gelgelar 250 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the Galactic Civil War,<ref name="Platt" /> which pitted the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] against each other between [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] discovered the only existing structure on the planet&mdash;the mysterious, abandoned Shrine of Kooroo&mdash;and camped nearby.<ref name="Platt" />

===The center of a town===
Eventually, the [[Colonist/Legends|settlers]] established the town of Gelgelar Free Port around the shrine, with [[Red Threxa's Boarding House]] and the [[Cantina/Legends|bar]] known as the [[Slippery Gelgelar Eel]] located in the adjacent buildings on the opposing sides of the structure. The locals of the Gelgelar Free Port generally avoided the shrine, but visiting [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] often sought out the [[Wise Man of Kooroo]], an eccentric [[Hermit/Legends|hermit]] who had come to reside in the sanctuary.<ref name="Platt" />

By the time of the Galactic Civil War, members of the [[Fellowship of Kooroo]], a cult dedicated to the worship of the Shrines of Kooroo, occasionally visited the shrine on Gelgelar as part of a [[Pilgrimage of Kooroo|pilgrimage]] to various sites throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] supposedly connected to the group's spiritual leader, [[Kooroo (being)|Kooroo]]. During their visits, the pilgrims<ref name="Platt" /> [[Meditation/Legends|meditated]]<ref name="Journal14 Shrines" /> in the shrine and conversed with the Wise Man of Kooroo. Whenever the pilgrims were in the Gelgelar Free Port, strange chanting and scented smoke emanated from the entrance of the shrine.<ref name="Platt" />

===Visits planned===
{{Quote|Exposing the secrets of the Shrine of Kooroo can only shatter its peace.|A group of pilgrims of Kooroo|<ref name="Platt" />}}
{{RPGseed}}
[[File:Wise_Man_of_Kooroo.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Professor Reina Solov hired a group of individuals to talk to the Wise Man of Kooroo (pictured).]]
Around that time, [[Reina Solov]], an [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeology]] [[Professor/Legends|professor]] from the prestigious [[University of Byblos/Legends|University of Byblos]] on the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] planet [[Byblos/Legends|Byblos]], hired a group of individuals. The group was to travel to Gelgelar and obtain information on the Shrine of Kooroo, including its origins and the source of the stone from which it was built.<ref name="Platt" />

Tasked with visiting the Wise Man of Kooroo, the individuals encountered a group of pilgrims at the shrine. The pilgrims warned the other group to stay away from the Shrine of Kooroo lest they disturb the peace of the sanctuary by exposing its secrets. Another group of spacers, noticing the interest in the shrine displayed by Solov's group, believed the individuals to be [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunters]]. Hoping to [[Thief/Legends|steal]] any artifacts recovered by Solov's group, the spacers followed and later ambushed the group.<ref name="Platt" />

On another occasion, a group of six pilgrims of Kooroo contracted a [[free-trader]] [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] to transport them to Gelgelar, where the pilgrims intended to visit the Shrine of Kooroo. In reality, however, one of the individuals posing as a pilgrim was the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Dorius Drevin]], intending to collect a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on [[Loro Ecls]], the unofficial [[Mayor/Legends|mayor]] of the Gelgelar Free Port. Drevin [[Death/Legends|killed]] one of the pilgrims, [[Gudren Lagarian]], while the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] was still in transit to Gelgelar, hiding [[Gender/Legends|his]] body in a maintenance shaft of the [[Starship/Legends|starship]]. The ship soon landed at the Gelgelar Free Port and released its passengers, and the free-[[Merchant/Legends|traders]] eventually became engaged in a [[Firefight in the Gelgelar Free Port|firefight]] when Drevin attacked Ecis.<ref name="Platt" />
{{Endgame}}

===Scholars and spies===
{{Quote|Scattered on remote planets in certain areas of the Outer Rim, the mysterious Shrines of Kooroo, all constructed of the same natural stone (even on Gelgelar, where the only stone around is meters or decameters deep subterranean bedrock), are a source of scholarly and popular interest.|Lecture by Dr. Corellia Antilles|<ref name="Journal14" />}}
Around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="1 ABY">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of "[[The Breath of Gelgelar]]" to approximately [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].</ref> the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[T'laerean Larn]] had learned from the Wise Man of Kooroo the [[Force power/Legends|ability]] to merge his consciousness and senses with an [[Sunshine (reeho)|animal]] by using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. When using the ability for the first time, Larn mused that soon he would be able to merge his mind with any animal or plant on Gelgelar. Larn further speculated that such mastery over the Force ability would allow him to let his mind wander around the Shrine of Kooroo and [[Spy/Legends|spy]] on the pilgrims present at the sanctuary.<ref name="Breath">{{JournalCite|14|The Breath of Gelgelar}}</ref> A [[2 ABY/Legends|year later]],<ref name="2 ABY">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}} &mdash; [[Andor Javin]] transmitted [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[NewsNet]] report mentioning Gelgelar's [[Shrine of Kooroo]], on the date 38:1:15, which corresponds to [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> the investigative [[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] [[Andor Javin]] mentioned the Gelgelar Shrine of Kooroo in a [[TriNebulon News/Legends|TriNebulon News]] report.<ref name="Journal13" /> The [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] also mentioned the shrine in a personal addendum to an entry on the Gelgelar Free Port in a document detailing various spaceports of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="Platt" />

The [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeologist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Henrietya Antilles|Corellia Antilles]] gave a lecture at the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Galactic Museum]] on<ref name="Journal14" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="Journal14" /> around 11 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]].<ref name="11 ABY" /> During the lecture, Antilles discussed the Shrines of Kooroo, including the fact that the structures had all been constructed of the same type of stone. She highlighted the unusual nature of this fact with regard to the Gelgelar shrine due to the highly limited accessibility of the material on that planet.<ref name="Journal14" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Wise Man of Kooroo}}
{{Quote|It was a good thing I came to the settlement earlier than I had planned.|The Wise Man of Kooroo, visiting T'laerean Larn in the Krevk Settlement|<ref name="Breath" />}}
[[File:WiseManOfKooroo-Journal14.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Wise Man of Kooroo resided at the Shrine of Kooroo.]]
By the time of its discovery, the Shrine of Kooroo on Gelgelar had been abandoned. That changed long before the Galactic Civil War, when the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]]<ref name="Platt" /> [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="Breath" /> Glovan Thule fled to Gelgelar for unknown reasons and settled there for life. Although some believed that Thule had been a [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi apprentice]],<ref name="Platt" /> he was in fact not a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] or even particularly skilled in the use of the Force.<ref name="Breath" />

Thule came to reside in the Shrine of Kooroo, where he sat in the center of the sanctuary on a pile of tattered animal skins. In such position, the hermit leaned on a [[Cane/Legends|cane]] and [[Smoking/Legends|smoked]] a [[Pipe/Legends|pipe]]. Thule adopted the name "Wise Man of Kooroo" and eventually forgot his original name. The pilgrims of Kooroo visiting the shrine believed the Wise Man to be a [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] of a long-forgotten religion, and he dispensed [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophical]] sayings and advice to any visitors.<ref name="Platt" />

The Wise Man subsisted on rainwater penetrating the exterior of the shrine and offerings of [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] by any visitors to the structure. In times when there were not many pilgrims visiting Gelgelar, [[Thulls]], the [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] proprietor of the nearby Slippery Gelgelar Eel bar, was observed bringing food to the Wise Man. Although the Wise Man himself was never seen leaving the shrine,<ref name="Platt" /> he did in fact visit the [[Krevk Settlement]] outside the Gelgelar Free Port, where his student, T'laerean Larn, lived, on at least one occasion.<ref name="Breath" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Shrine of Kooroo was first introduced in the [[1995]] [[West End Games]] [[roleplaying game]] sourcebook ''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]'', which was authored by [[Peter M. Schweighofer|Peter Schweighofer]]. In the book, the shrine was illustrated by [[Chris Gossett]]. ''Platt's Starport Guide'' includes several adventure seeds for use with ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. This article assumes the scenarios play out as described.<ref name="Platt" />
